To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the capacity to aspire of future Indonesian internal migrants is already significantly higher than that of non-migrants before migration, (2) migration further increases the capacity to aspire, and (3) the aspiration gap between migrants and non-migrant is not only due to the economic benefits of migration, but is also partly due to a certain disposition of migrants to have higher aspirations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ‘capacity to aspire’, i.e. a personal disposition to aspire to higher economic outcomes, is a key factor in explaining the higher aspirations of migrants, and that this capacity to aspire is a crucial factor in explaining the high aspirations of migrants.
the aspiration gap between migrants and non-migrant Indonesians is not caused by migration but rather the other way around.
